title: Reliable or Fast: Acknowledgements, Retransmission and a Window

questions.question: What does an acknowledgement of 3 tell the sender?
options: The next one the receiver expects is 3: everything below it has arrived
Packet 3 has arrived, and nothing is known about the ones before it
Packet 3 was lost and should be sent again at once
Three packets have arrived in total, in whatever order
questions.explanation: The number is the first one still missing. Because it covers everything below it, a lost acknowledgement is made good by the next one.

questions.question: A receiver gets packets 2, 0, 1, 1, 0. What does it deliver?
options: c a b b a, in the order they came, with nothing held back
a b c, and then b and a again, since repeats may carry new data
Only a, since 2 arrived out of order and the stream was abandoned
a b c, once each and in order, with 2 duplicates counted: 2 waited until 0 and 1 had come
questions.explanation: An early packet waits for the gap before it to fill, and a repeat is ignored but still acknowledged, because the sender may have lost the first acknowledgement.

questions.question: What does the window do?
options: Sets how long the sender waits before resending: window 4 means four ticks
Limits how many unacknowledged packets are on the wire: window 4 with ten messages sent 4, then nothing until an acknowledgement freed room
Orders the packets at the receiver: window 4 holds four early packets until the gap fills
Limits the size of each packet: window 4 with ten messages split them into four packets
questions.explanation: Without a limit a sender could flood a slow link. With one, new packets go out only as acknowledgements make room.

questions.question: 500 messages over a link that loses 20 percent each way. What did sending once deliver, and what did reliable cost?
options: 398 delivered at 1.00 packets per message, against 500 delivered at 1.79 packets per message
500 delivered at 1.00 packets per message by both: reliable costs nothing when it works
398 delivered at 1.79 packets per message, against 500 at 1.00
320 delivered at 1.00 packets per message, against 500 at 2.50
questions.explanation: A fifth of single sends are lost. Reliable loses none, and pays in resends, some of them for packets that did arrive but whose acknowledgement did not.

questions.question: With a one way delay of 50 ticks, how long did 100 messages take at a window of 1 and of 10?
options: 1000 ticks and 10000 ticks: a wider window has more to wait for
10000 ticks for both: the delay sets the time, not the window
10000 ticks and 1000 ticks: a window of one is one message per round trip
5000 ticks and 500 ticks
questions.explanation: A window of 1 waits a full round trip of 100 ticks for each message. Ten at a time is ten per round trip.

questions.question: When is reliable the wrong choice for a topic?
options: For a command such as stop, which must not be delayed by waiting for an acknowledgement
For a stream such as scans that is replaced by the next message: it spends the retransmissions on data that is already stale and adds load to a link in trouble
For a parameter that is set once, since one message is not worth the bookkeeping
Never: a message that was worth sending is worth delivering
questions.explanation: A lost scan is replaced by the next one a moment later. Resending the old one adds load exactly when the link is in trouble, for data nobody wants any more.
